Advisor to Thrall{{questlong|Horde|28|A Unknown Letter}} | location = [[Stormbreaker Point]], [[Balor]] | status = Alive }} '''Kilrogg Deadeye''' is the chieftain of the [[Bleeding Hollow clan]]. Leading his clan in both the [[First War|First]] and [[Second War]]s, Kilrogg was one of the older and more cunning orc chieftains. ==Background== ===First War=== As an older chieftain, Kilrogg Deadeye had become more unwilling to throw lives away in combat. In orcish politics older orcs become more pragmatic, which is often mistaken for cowardice by the younger generation. Prior to the sacking of Stormwind, Kilrogg had killed three of his sons and two grandsons already who thought they could rule the clan better.''The Last Guardian'', pg. 221 At the start of the First War, the Bleeding Hollow clan participated in the first attack on [[Stormwind Keep]], along with the [[Twilight's Hammer clan]] led by [[Cho'gall]]. This first attack was an unmitigated disaster for the orcs, and Deadeye loudly proclaimed that the attack had failed due to Cho'gall's incompetence. A rift soon grew that threatened to rip the Horde apart before it had even begun its conquest of Azeroth, as the orcs quickly polarized into factions that supported either chieftain. [[Gul'dan]] quickly stepped in to quell the problem, installing [[Blackhand]] as Warchief of the Horde to restore order to the Horde.''Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness'' manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_II:_Tides_of_Darkness_manual#The_Mastery_of_Forces_-_Medivh_and_Blackhand The History of Orcish Ascension]'', The Mastery of Forces - Medivh and Blackhand ===Second War and aftermath=== [[File:Kilrogg.png|thumb|right|Kilrogg during the Second War.]] Kilrogg fought under [[Blackhand]], and then later under [[Orgrim Doomhammer]]. During the war, his clan was stationed throughout [[Khaz Modan]], where it controlled the Horde's vital mining and oil refining operations.''Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness'' manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_II:_Tides_of_Darkness_manual#Bleeding_Hollow_Clan Clans of the Horde]'', Bleeding Hollow Clan After the tide of the Second War turned and the Horde was defeated, Kilrogg managed to lead his clan back through the rift of the [[Dark Portal]] and into [[Draenor]]. There he was hailed as a hero, and was taken before [[Ner'zhul]]. After recounting the events of the Second War to the old shaman, Kilrogg, along with [[Grommash Hellscream]] and [[Kargath Bladefist]], led the charge back into Azeroth to steal items of power needed to aid Ner'zhul in his scheme to retrieve certain artifacts from Azeroth as to open rifts into other worlds and take the Orcish Hordes to great victories beyond the Dark Portal.''Warcraft II: Beyond the Dark Portal'' game manual, [https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_II:_Beyond_the_Dark_Portal_manual#The_Aftermath_of_the_Second_War The Aftermath of the Second War] When Ner'zhul used the items to open more portals, Hellscream and Deadeye realized Ner'zhul's mad plans would doom their entire race. They abandoned Ner'zhul and rallied as many orcs as they could find, driving them through the Dark Portal to the questionable safety of Azeroth just before Draenor was destroyed.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Invasion_of_Draenor The Invasion of Draenor] Their clans passed through just before Archmage [[Khadgar]] closed it completely. Hellscream and Deadeye hacked their way through the human ranks in a desperate bid for freedom, the Dark Portal exploding behind them. For them, and the remaining orcs on Azeroth, there would be no going back.''Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos'' game manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_III:_Reign_of_Chaos_Game_Manual#Ner'zhul_and_the_Shadow_Clans Orcish History]'', Ner'zhul and the Shadow Clans Though Grom Hellscream and his [[Warsong clan]] managed to evade capture, Deadeye and his Bleeding Hollow clan were rounded up and placed in the internment camps in Lordaeron.''Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos'' game manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_III:_Reign_of_Chaos_Game_Manual#Day_of_the_Dragon Orcish History]'', Day of the Dragon[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Battle_of_Grim_Batol_(History_of_Warcraft) The Battle of Grim Batol] The captive clans, including the Bleeding Hollow, were eventually freed by [[Thrall]], son of [[Durotan]]. Supported by many of the veteran chieftains, presumably including Kilrogg, Thrall ultimately succeeded in revitalizing the Horde and giving his people a new spiritual identity.''Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos'' Game Manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_III:_Reign_of_Chaos_Game_Manual#Thrall's_Tale Orcish History]'', Thrall's Tale[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_New_Horde The New Horde] Kilrogg would go on to serve as an advisor to the young warchief, and members of his clan would later occupy the outpost of [[Grom'gol Base Camp]] in the Stranglethorn Vale.A Bleeding Hollow banner can be found next to [[Far Seer Mok'thardin]]. ===Mysteries of Azeroth=== On Thrall's orders, Kilrogg led his clan to the island of [[Balor]], where the Bleeding Hollow established the outpost of [[Stormbreaker Point]] from which to hunt the Shadow Council and the remains of the [[Stormreaver clan]] that had begun to inhabit the ruins once more. ==Quests== * {{questlong|Horde|28|A Unknown Letter}} {{questfinish}} * {{questlong|Horde|30|Bugs on My Island}} {{queststartfinish}} * {{questlong|Horde|31|Deep in the Mines}} {{queststartfinish}} * {{questlong|Horde|32|Eyes of Stormreaver}} {{queststartfinish}} * {{questlong|Horde|33|Mere Thoughts}} {{queststartfinish}} * {{questlong|Horde|35+|Colony of Ants}} {{queststartfinish}} * {{questlong|Horde|38D|It Can't Rain All the Time}} {{queststartfinish}} * {{questlong|Horde|38|Storm's End}} {{queststart}} ==Quotes== ===Gossip=== A question aches at the back of my mind: Has this world truly forgotten me? All that I was-lost, by choice or fate. Wherever I turn my gaze, I see nothing. Nothing. This New Horde, our people's future, abandoned me. But I will not abandon it. Many sang my death to bury the past. Yet here I stand, ready to end what remains of Gul'dan's misery. I feel duty, but also jealousy. What sets me apart from Grommash Hellscream? Were his final acts so grand that they erased his past? I recall when his name was sung as hero, while I was dismissed as an elder. Perhaps it is unbecoming of me to feel this way, but I will not fade. My name will stand among legends-not by death, but by atonement. The Shadow Council will face the wrath of my clan, my ancestors, and MY MIGHT. Lok-tar-ogar! For the Horde! ===On-click=== ;Greeting * For the Horde! * Beware the shadows of this place. * By my axe, victory or death! ;Farewell * Show them no mercy! ;Pissed * Your mind is as hollow as my eye. * Is chatter all you are good for? * A disappointment to the Horde. ==Trivia== * The warlock spell Eye of Kilrogg is named after the renowned chieftain.''Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness'' manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_II:_Tides_of_Darkness_manual#Ogre-Mage_Spells Ogre-Mage Spells]'' However, Kilrogg himself feels insulted by the name.{{questlong|Horde|32|Eyes of Stormreaver}} * The [[Deadeye Shore]] in [[Durotar]] is named after Kilrogg. ==Patch changes== * {{Patch|1.18.0|note=Added.}} ==References== {{reflist}} {{Succession|Unknown|'''[[Bleeding Hollow clan|Chieftain of the Bleeding Hollow clan]]'''|Incumbent}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Deadeye, Kilrogg}} [[Category:Orc characters]] [[Category:Bleeding Hollow clan]] [[Category:Balor NPCs]] [[Category:Quest givers]]
